help.title: How to Trade Cards in Pokemon TCG Pocket: Guide & FAQ
help.description: How trading works in Pokemon TCG Pocket: which cards can be traded, what they cost in Shinedust, what replaced Trade Tokens, and how to find players to trade with online.
help.heading: How to trade cards in Pokemon TCG Pocket
help.intro: Welcome to <site>pokemon-tcg.exchange</site>, the exchange center for Pokemon TCG Pocket players! This guide explains how trading works in the game, and how the site finds you players to trade with online.

rules.heading: How trading works in the game
items: You can only trade with players on your friends list.
Both cards must have the same rarity: a ◊◊ card for another ◊◊ card.
Some cards cannot be traded: ☆☆☆ cards, crown cards and promo cards.
From ◊◊◊ up, a trade costs Shinedust, to both players.
Every trade uses trade stamina, which comes back with time or with trade hourglasses.
Both players have to accept the trade.

site.heading: How to find players to trade with online
site.intro: The game only lets you trade with friends, and does not help you find them. That is what <site>pokemon-tcg.exchange</site> is for:
items: Your wishlist: select the cards you want.
Your offers: select the cards you can give.
Your Friend ID: the players who match with you add you as a friend with it.
Your matches: the site finds the players who give what you want, and want what you give.
Your trades: see the proposals, talk with the other players, and update your lists at any time.
site.outro: The trade itself is made in the game, between friends. The site is free, and never asks for your game account.

steps.heading: How to use the site, step by step

wants.title: Select the cards you want
wants.text: Browse every Pokemon TCG Pocket card, and filter by set, rarity or name to find the ones you miss.
wants.alt: The cards you are looking for

offers.title: Select the cards you can offer
offers.text: Add the duplicates you can trade away. The more you offer, the more matches you get. With a joker, you give all your cards of one rarity in a set with a single click, except the ones you want.

friendId.title: Enter your Friend ID
friendId.text: Your Friend ID is a 16-digit number of Pokemon TCG Pocket. To find it:
items: tap your avatar or your name in the game,
your Friend ID is at the top of your profile,
enter it on the site, without hyphens.
friendId.alt: The Friend ID on the profile screen

matches.title: Get matches and proposals
matches.text: The site compares your lists with those of the other players. For each match, you see:
items: the cards you can trade, and what they cost in Shinedust,
the pseudonym and Friend ID of the other player, with a QR code to add them,
when they last came, and a way to write to them.

account.title: Keep your account up to date
account.text: Choose the same pseudonym and icon as in the game, say which rarities you accept to trade, and edit your lists as your collection grows.

packs.heading: Which booster packs to open
packs.text: In the Insights menu of your account, the site counts the cards of your wishlist in each booster pack:
items: see at a glance which packs hold the most cards you miss,
open the right ones first, and trade for the others.
packs.alt: The best packs for your wishlist

list.question: How do I exchange Trade Tokens in Pokemon TCG Pocket?
list.answer: Trade Tokens no longer exist: Shinedust replaced them in July 2025, and the tokens the players had were turned into Shinedust. Trades are now paid in Shinedust.

list.question: How do I get Shinedust?
list.answer: You get Shinedust when you obtain a card you already have, and from missions and events.

list.question: Which cards cannot be traded?
list.answer: Cards with three stars (immersive), crown cards and promo cards cannot be traded. The site shows them with 🚫, and leaves them out of the proposals.

list.question: Can I trade with any player online?
list.answer: Only with your friends in the game. When the site finds you a match, add the other player with their Friend ID or their QR code, then start the trade in the game.

list.question: How do I find my Friend ID?
list.answer: Tap your avatar or your name in the game: your Friend ID is at the top of your profile. Enter its 16 digits on the site, without hyphens.

list.question: Why do First Partners (SP1) cards have their own proposals?
list.answer: Cards of the First Partners special pack are only traded for cards of the same pack, so the site matches them apart.

list.question: Can I exchange pack points for cards?
list.answer: Yes, in the game: opening packs of a set gives you points, which you spend on a card of that set. Tap a card on the site to see how many points it costs.

list.question: Can I change my wishlist or my offers later?
list.answer: Yes, at any time from your account. Up-to-date lists give you better matches.

list.question: How do I delete my account?
list.answer: At the bottom of the Account page. Your lists, your email, your password and your Friend ID are deleted for good.
